policy: Retain noisy recordings unchanged. Background-noise annotation does not override acoustic timing QC or qualify an RIR.

runs.label: Background noise present
runs.basis: User reports unavoidable background noise; recorded pre-excitation audio and prior level analysis support this annotation.

noise_reference_windows.name: pre_excitation_background
noise_reference_windows.qualification: Conservative initial background window, before the earliest start-marker search region. Inspect for transient noise before estimating a noise spectrum.

noise_reference_windows.name: late_post_excitation_candidate
noise_reference_windows.qualification: Candidate only: verify final-marker and room decay have reached the background floor. Do not automatically treat the sweep decay or marker ringing as noise.

later_processing: Verify source hashes and resolve acoustic sweep timing before RIR extraction.
Use background-only audio to estimate per-microphone noise spectra, not as a waveform to subtract.
Evaluate time-varying noise and reject contaminated reference windows; do not assume pre/post noise is stationary.
Preserve genuine room decay and inter-microphone timing and level relationships.
Keep original audio and unprocessed RIR. Store any denoised RIR separately with parameters and before/after quality checks.
Background-only segments cannot guarantee removal of nonstationary speech or recovery of masked room decay.
